correctness.rationale: The orbit barycenter construction is an explicit PL homeomorphism to the genuine fixed set. Exhaustive Hamming-distance casework identifies the orbit flag graph and cone links. Each link is the union of two simplices and m+1 matching edges, homotopy equivalent to m circles. The m attaching loops at each z give edge-difference relations x_w x_z^{-1} in the free bridge group, because each copy VR(Q_m;2) is simply connected (indeed a 3-sphere wedge or simplex). A spanning-tree choice eliminates 2^m-1 bridge 1-cells by integral CW cell cancellation; the remaining m*2^m-(2^m-1) 2-cells give the stated S^2 rank. The published integral VR(Q_m;2) theorem supplies two c_m S^3 wedges. Replayed full small-complex enumerations and signed Lefschetz checks are consistent and not extrapolated as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The full-text accessible 2026 ambient-character analysis arXiv:2606.20784 yields rational ambient hyperoctahedral representations and therefore a Lefschetz fixed Euler characteristic, not a geometric fixed-point homotopy type. The earlier Adamaszek--Adams scale-two wedge theorem applies to the two lower-cube subcomplexes but cannot identify the transposition-fixed orbit complex or its cone-attachment maps. The 2026 toric-cohomology work studies ambient cohomology; Feng studies ambient scale three. A separately examined coordinate-flip fixed-locus result has a nonconjugate involution with zero fixed cube vertices. value.rationale: A coordinate transposition is a fundamental natural hypercube symmetry, and its geometric fixed locus cannot be reconstructed from ambient rational representation ranks or Euler characteristics. The all-dimension theorem exposes exponentially many fixed-locus S^2 classes invisible in the ambient scale-two complex, identifies independent S^3 classes for n>=5, and supplies reusable exact orbit and cone-link models. This is a complete integral homotopy classification of a motivated infinite family, not a restatement of ambient sphere counts or a small finite calculation.
